title: A hidden base's way in is an airlock a guard watches: two blast doors 264 apart, a booth with a camera, a check that takes half a minute
rule: From outside the way into a dug-in base is a plain door in the wall it is cut into, with only a few drums, pallets and a fence by it. Behind it: an airlock about 208 wide, 175 high and 264 to 272 between its doors; the outer door two leaves sliding apart quickly, the inner one slower and heavier; a keypad about 52 up beside each door. A small booth (about 115 by 192, ceiling 96) looks into it, with a screen fed by a camera over the outer door and monitors angled at the seat. Letting someone in is a show of about 30 s: spray, smoke, a scan, then the inner door opens. Our bunker's sliding door is settled (the owner liked it, 19 November): an airlock in front of it, or a guard's check at the way in, is new and changes how players enter a base: ask the owner first.
why: d1_eli_01 (21 November): outer doors_Airlock_Outside and b, func_door movedir 0 and 180, speed 100, lip 8, wait 4, each under a blastdoor001a or b prop; inner airlock_door and b at speed 40 and 50, lip 12; doors at y 2872 and 2608 (264 apart), 208 wide inside, ceiling 173. The second airlock (to the scrapyard, d1_eli_01 and 02): doors at y 1160 and 888 (272 apart), 208 wide, ceiling 177, speed 25 to 45, its own booth at x -720. Booth: ceiling 96, 115 by 192, controlroom_monitor001b pitched 30, four monitor01b pitched 37 to 54 and turned 7 to 47 toward the seat; point_camera camera_mossman_airlock over the door feeds func_monitor monitor_airlock_entrance; env_microphone mic_airlockMossman. 21 keypad prop_dynamics in the two maps, 48 to 54 over the floor (median 53), 14 to 64 from a door leaf. Outside the door: the dam's own concrete (concretewall064b, c, d: 59% of walls within 2000), gravel and red grass, and 15 props: 5 oil drums, 4 fence pieces, 3 pallets, 2 crates, a garbage pile.
how: Map modules: an `airlock` piece for a Resistance site (two door pairs 264 apart named lc_airlock_outer and lc_airlock_inner, a booth with lc_airlock_cam pointed at the outer door, keypads 52 up), the outer front dressed like the wall it sits in. Gamemode: the Resistance's guard (a player or the quartermaster) opens the inner door from the booth; the 30 s check (steam, a hum, a light sweeping) plays as sound and effects, never as text.
check: map_lint: an airlock piece whose doors are under 192 apart, or a door with no keypad or button within 64

title: Guns that seem to follow you are props: six floor cells choose where they aim
rule: When a defence only has to look alive (turrets over a door, a camera that turns), make it a prop with aiming animations and lay a grid of touch triggers on the floor: each cell plays the aim for that cell, and the aiming sound's pitch is picked at random from three each time. The guns drop from ceiling panels when the place is on guard and go back when the guard lets you in. Turrets that shoot are another thing (valve-turret-pairs).
why: d1_eli_01 airlock (21 November): two labturret prop_dynamics behind func_door panels (speed 175, lip 2, opened by logic_turrets_1_deploy, shut 2.2 s after retract); six trigger_multiple Trigger_Prox_turrets in two columns of three (centres x -124 and 8, y 2646, 2744, 2846: cells about 132 by 100), each OnStartTouch > prop_turret_1_L SetAnimation aimN and prop_turret_1_R aim_MN (0 to 0.3 s apart) and > Case_turrets_variety PickRandom, which sets ambient_sound_turrets_1_aim to pitch 200, 215 or 230. A glow sprite on each gun's light attachment. Retracted when Mossman opens his blast door (lcs_airlock01 OnTrigger2).
how: Gamemode: a fixture 'Turret, watching' for the Resistance's way in (props_lab/labturret.mdl) that turns toward the nearest stranger in its cone a few times a second (in Lua no grid is needed), with a whir at a random pitch, and folds away when a member is near. New: ask the owner before adding it to a base.

title: A long lift ride down into a base shows its life floor by floor
rule: When the way into a base goes down a long way, use the ride: an open cage in a shaft that passes floors you can see into but not reach (sleeping quarters, a kitchen, a workshop), each with a few people at work started just before it comes into view and removed once the lift is past. The floor ahead is opened to sight as the lift reaches it and the one behind is shut a moment later. A guide rides along. A lift, or floors only seen, would be new to our bases: ask the owner first.
why: d1_eli_01 (21 November): func_tracktrain elevator_lab (startspeed 65) carrying a freightelevator prop on seven path_tracks from z -1214 to -2672 (1458, about 22 s); shaft 176 by 800, 1456 high. Floors passed at z -1584 (dormitory), -1872 (kitchen), -2160 (repairs): 288 apart, no AI nodes on any of them, only elevatordoor props as gates. elevator_trigger_go_up_1 starts them on the ride's clock: logic_loungers_start @4, logic_kitchenscene_start @6.5, logic_RepairmenScene_Start @14.2, lift Resume @3. path_tracks 2a, 2b, 2c: OnPass > portal_elevator_ride_N+1 Open @0 and portal_elevator_ride_N Close @3. The last stop: shake, ding @1, doors open, logic_KILL_EM_ALL KillHierarchy on the vignettes' NPCs. The lift moves only once the guide is in (trigger_once for NPCs enabling the player's trigger).
how: Map modules: a `lift` piece (a func_tracktrain or func_movelinear cage, doors of two leaves at top and bottom, lip 16, speed 100, wait 4) with lc_life_N spots on the floors it passes. Gamemode: life spots on a passing floor are filled when a rider is within reach and emptied after, like the camps' fighters who slip away out of sight (city.md).
check: map_lint: each areaportal a lift opens on the way is shut again by a later stop

title: A Resistance base is shown at work: cooks with their tools, sleepers, a game of chess, vortigaunts mending with their beams
rule: Fill the base with work, each person on his own spot with the tools in his hands: two cooks at a stove (a hat on the head, a ladle or a cleaver in the hand, put there as the scene starts), one man asleep on a bed and two at a chess table in the quarters, vortigaunts zapping a broken machine in short bursts, a lab worker at his bench who stops when spoken to and goes back after, and one person walking a loop between two places with a pause at each end. Changes how our camps' people behave: ask the owner first.
why: d1_eli_01 (21 November): vortigaunts sheffy_soup and sheffy_butcher on scripted_sequences soupstir and Butcher, sheffyhat, sheffyLadel and sheffyCleaver prop_dynamics put on by SetParentAttachment (hat, ladel_attachment, cleaver_attachment) in logic_kitchenscene_start; cit_lounger02 on SS Lying_Down over a prison bed, cit__lounger01 on Sit_Chair and vort__lounger01 on chess_Pose 48 apart across props_lab/chess; vort_repairman_01 and 02 made to hate npc_bullseye bullseye_repairman1 (ApplyRelationship @0 and @0.75, Revert @6, the scene removed @7); Eli, Mossman, Alyx and the lab vort each on a work loop scene that a talk pauses (busyactor 1) and resumes after; the walker: SS_bgwalker1 OnEndSequence > SS_bgwalker2 @3, its end > SS_bgwalker1 @6. 7 vortigaunts and 5 citizens in the map, none idle.
how: Gamemode: the camps' fighters and the vortigaunts (loyalty-and-vortigaunts.md) could take work spots from the editor ('Point: cook', 'Point: mend', 'Point: chess', 'Point: sleep') with a prop parented to the hand while there; a mending vortigaunt plays its beam at the spot's machine every few seconds. Map modules: lc_busy_cook, lc_busy_mend and lc_busy_chess points in kitchens, workshops and quarters (valve-npc-busy-poses).

title: Give players a moment to look round, and let the person there answer what they look at
rule: After a talk, leave a short free moment (about 25 s) in which a person in the room says something about whatever a player stops to look at: a photo, a machine, a board on the wall. Looking means within reach (70 to 190) and the thing near the middle of the view (a cone of 32 to 80 degrees) for half a second to a second. Once one is said the others are dropped and things move on. Spoken, never written. New: ask the owner first.
why: d1_eli_01 (21 November): four ai_script_conditions for Eli, enabled @0.7 to 1.5 by logic_timer_lookaround_enable_1 and switched off @25 by a kill switch: conditions_photo (frame002a, within 120, cone 32, 0.5 s), conditions_teleport (190, 80, 0.5 s), conditions_thing (70, 35, 0.5 s), conditions_breen (corkboard002, 150, 35, 1 s). OnConditionsSatisfied starts that line once and disables the other three; each line ends by resuming Eli's work loop.
how: Gamemode: a base's quartermaster or a vortigaunt answers a player who looks at a marked thing ('Point: talking point' with a recorded line, recorded-lines.md) for 0.7 s within 150 and a 40 degree cone, once a player in 10 minutes. No text.

title: The Combine's attack on a base is told by the base itself, and comes at a moment nobody chose
rule: When the Combine hit the Resistance's base, the base tells it: a blast and a shake far off, emergency lamps blinking and a fire bell, the screen in the booth breaking into static and going dark, doors shutting behind the defenders, scanners and canisters over the yard, and only then the first enemy inside. Part of the base can be lost to a cave-in. It starts at a random moment in a window of minutes, not on a clock players can learn. The raid on a base is not built (resistance-base.md): ask the owner first.
why: d1_eli_02 (21 November): timer_attack refire 80, upper bound 180, fires once during the scrapyard play. logic_attack_start: scenes @0, battlefx_0 @8 (six env_particlescript scanner swarms, three npc_cscanner on aiscripted_schedules, env_headcrabcanister HCC1 to 4 @4, 9, 12, 15, chopper_flyby_04 @12), battlefx_1 @12 (shake, explode_9, the battle loop @3, explode_2 @12). lcs_attack01: scrapyard gate @12, airlock @14, rockets armed @20. trigger_attack02 shuts the airlock behind. lcs_attack02: Eli on monitor_airlock_south, then monitor_airlock_south_noise on for 0.5 s, later for 7 s, and the off brush. logic_start_fighting_1: cop_fight_maker against vort_fight_maker, cops_vs_Eli_ignore. The cave-in (battlefx_3, trigger_cavein): breakable_rockfall_2 @0.5, physboxes dropped @1, rope_L_5 Break @1 with sparks, rock showers @1 and @3.5, dust @0.5 and @3, a ceiling func_door (speed 450, lip -128) closing @2. sound_firebell_1 loop on lcs_attack01's end.
how: Gamemode (when the owner wants raids on the base): the HQ's monitors show static, its lamps blink and a bell rings for the defenders; far blasts and a shake reach everyone in the base; units arrive 20 to 60 s later through the way in; the start chosen at random within a few minutes of the order. Map modules: lc_hq_alarm lamps and an lc_hq_bell sound in the HQ pieces.

title: Teach a tool by play: someone reacts to every try, lost things come back, and a goal shows when it is hit
rule: To teach a tool, give players something to play with and a person (or animal) who reacts: pleased when they catch or carry it, let down when it breaks. Throwables that break or get lost come back from where they came. A goal (a hoop, a target) is a pair of touch zones, the upper one arming the lower for a second, so only a real score counts; a hit lights a sprite and gets one word of praise. The first real test opens the way on; a way round it opens anyway if they cannot (valve-teach-then-give-up). Fits our job games (house rule 9).
why: d1_eli_02 scrapyard (21 November): 10 dogobject crates each from an env_entity_maker (maker_box1 to 10) with its point_template; w_1_obj_N OnPhysGunPickup > logic_C_yes_N (Alyx's praise picked by a logic_case), OnBreak > logic_C_no_N (lcs_dog_dissapointed). Ball from maker_ball; trigger_Ball_vent and trigger_lost_ball_top start 'where's the ball' and break it @6 so the maker makes another. Hoop: trigger_BBall_score_top enables trigger_BBall_score_bottom, which is disabled again 1 s after the ball leaves the top; a score shows Sprite_score for 2 s and lcs_al_niceshot once. timer_fetch 60 s: Alyx suggests fetch if nobody has played. First test: a ledge 130 up beside the gate button (trigger_scrap_1st_success unlocks button_scrapyard_gate); env_speaker AlyxStackNag 12 to 24 s.
how: Gamemode job games: a crate-stacking or catch game for the Resistance's recruits where a vortigaunt or the quartermaster reacts aloud to each try; props a game uses come back from a spawn spot when broken or lost; any goal made of two zones. No text beyond the one key.

title: A base dug into the ground is one plain concrete, banded low, hung with salvage
rule: Build the Resistance's underground rooms in one plain board-marked concrete for walls, floors and ceilings alike, with a lower band of a second concrete to 112 or 128 (the owner's two tones hold here too), rubber mats on the lab floor, and dress it with what was carried in: runs of pipe props along walls and ceilings, chain-link frames standing as partitions, the prison's tube and cage lamps, a keypad by every door. Labs are higher than homes (ceilings 320 to 432). Light the work rooms a pale green fluorescent and dim, the quarters warmer and brighter, with plaster and painted walls. Where our bunker or cave office differs, ask the owner first.
why: d1_eli_01 (21 November): concretewall002a on 4610 of 15794 faces; in the lower lab 46% of wall, 55% of floor and 50% of ceiling area; rubberfloor009a 14% of the lab floor; first wall change at 112 on 422 and at 128 on 565 of 2412 walls (concretewall002c or 020a below, 002a above). 147 pipe props (93% square), 70 fence props (interior_fence002a to e, 001g; 91% square), 29 prison_flourescentlight001a, 22 prison_cagedlight001a, 7 walllight001a, 21 keypads in the two maps. Main lab 304 to 554 by 800 to 874, ceiling 320 to 432; Mossman's room 304 by 216, ceiling 128. Lower lab light: 37 light_spots and 6 lights, the commonest colour 169 205 188 (18 of them), median brightness 140, no styled light. Quarters: median 700, 232 213 174 and 202 222 165; walls concretewall002c 36%, concretewall021c 17%, plasterwall030c 15%; ceilings concreteceiling003a and plasterceiling006a.
how: Map tools: a `base` palette for Resistance interiors under ground (walls concrete/concretewall002a over 002c to 128, floors 002a with rubberfloor009a mats, ceilings 002a), pipes and interior_fence002 frames as dressing, keypads 52 up beside doors, lights 169 205 188 at about 140 in work rooms.
check: map_modules_check: a Resistance interior with no material change between 96 and 136 over its floor

title: The Resistance's quarters by their props: a dormitory of prison beds, a kitchen of fridges, a rec corner
rule: A base's dormitory is a row of prison bed frames, some side by side 52 apart, each with a mattress that sags on it, lockers in a row 48 apart along one wall, an armchair, a couch and a table. The kitchen is four fridges, counters, two stoves, two sinks and shelves along the walls with the middle clear. A rec corner is a chess table and a cafeteria table with its bench. Rooms are low (ceiling 128 to 200).
why: d1_eli_01 (21 November): dormitory at z -1584 (864 by 160 to 576, ceiling 128 to 200): 7 prison_bedframe001a (pairs at y 2068 and 2120, 2060 and 2112: 52 apart), 8 FurnitureMattress001a as prop_ragdoll, 4 lockers001a at x 208, 256, 304 (48 apart) and 496, furniturearmchair001a 2, furniturecouch001a, furniture_vanity01a, furnituretable003a with props_lab/chess, chair_office01a, cafeteria_table001a and 2 cafeteria_bench001a. Kitchen at z -1872 (504 by 736, ceiling 200): kitchen_fridge001a 4 (not solid), kitchen_counter001d 4 and 001a 2, kitchen_stove002a 2 and 001a, sinkkitchen01a 2, kitchen_shelf001a 2, soupprep, headcrabprep.
how: Map modules: the bunker's bunk room and the cave office's bunk room take this kit (beds in pairs 52 apart, lockers 48 apart); a kitchen kit for the HQ town. Use mattresses as loose props on the frames where a ragdoll is not wanted.

extra.how: Black Mesa East's scrapyard (d1_eli_02): the gravity gun nag starts 12 s after Alyx lays it out; the stacking nag every 12 to 24 s; reaching the ledge unlocks the gate button, and a failsafe opens the gate @7 anyway; walking past the lesson (trigger_skip_training) cancels and kills 17 pending lines at once; one env_hudhint (the swap key) is the only text in both Black Mesa East maps.

The Resistance's own (d1_eli_01, Mossman's room, 304 by 216): a securitybank beside servers against one wall, one button stepping four cameras of rooms nobody walks (cam_chefy the kitchen, cam_recroom, cam_foyer, cam_stairs); a fifth camera over the outer airlock door feeds the guard's booth while he lets someone in. In d1_eli_02 the airlock monitor carries Eli's call and breaks to static (a noise brush for 0.5 s, then 7 s) when the attack hits. Our HQ's securitybank could show the base's own way in: ask the owner first.

Black Mesa East's alarm (d1_eli_02) has no turning beacon: four lights with glow sprites blink on a relay that calls itself (on 1.2 s, off @1.2, again @1.9) over a fire bell loop (eli_lab.firebell_loop_1, flags 16).

A sky full of scanners is particles (d1_eli_02): six env_particlescript citadel_scanners set to loop, and only three real npc_cscanner on aiscripted_schedule paths; all removed by one relay (logic_kill_scanners) when players go back inside.
Underground too (d1_eli_01, Black Mesa East): the first change is at 112 on 422 walls and 128 on 565 of 2412, concretewall002c or 020a below plain 002a.
